To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the highest ethanol yields were obtained after rye pretreatment at 2.0 wt% of sulfuric acid, using coculture of pentose fermenters, and hydrolysis in hemicellulolytic prehydrolysate, reaching 9.4g/L of ethanol, which corresponds to 55% theoretical yield.
rye straw can be efficiently converted into bioethanol by using a combination of dilute acid prehydrolysis, enzymatic hydrolyzation and fermentation.

the highest ethanol production from rye straw was obtained after its pretreatment at 2.0 % (wt/vol) sulfuric acid and saccharification with 25 FPU enzymes/g cellulose in sodium citrate, followed by fermentation using a mixture of S. cerevisiae and C. tropicalis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dilution acid pretreatment with sulfuric acid concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 [wt/vol]% on saccharification and SHF or SHCF processes.
the effect of acid pretreatment on rye straw saccharification and ethanol yield.
the optimization of the pretreatment conditions and saccharification process of rye straw, which is an important raw material of the biofuel production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dilute acid pretreated rye straw, after enzymatic saccharifications in sodium citrate and fermentation in monoculture and coculture, is a potential feedstock to produce ethanol.

dilute acid pretreatments with sulfuric acid concentrations between 1.5 and 2.0 % (wt/vol), followed by enzymatic hydrolyses using enzymes dosage of at least 25 FPU /g cellulose, and SHCF processes using cocultures, are promising for the production of ethanol from rye straw.

the pretreatment of rye straw using dilute sulfuric acid at 1.0% [vol/vol] and subsequent enzymatic sacchariﬁcation in sodium citrate is an effective method for ethanol production from lignocellulosic biomass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dilute acid pretreatments of rye straw at 1.0 1.5 % H2SO4 are the optimal conditions for the subsequent enzymatic saccharifications and fermentation.

dilute acid pretreatments of rye straw are efficient methods for the production of ethanol from rye straw, and that the highest yields of fermentation are achieved by performing enzymatic saccharifications and fermentation in hemicelluloses prehydrolysates.
dilute acid pretreatments of rye straw at 1.0 1.5 % [wt/vol], using 1.5 2 h of reaction time at 120oC and 1.5 bar, are suitable for SHCF processes using cocultures.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of dilute acid prehydrolysate as a medium for cellulose hydrolysis is not recommended for rye straw pretreated with 1.5 2% [wt/volsulfuric acid, as it leads to the inhibition of enzymatic saccharifications and ethanol fermentation.
the use of dilute acid prehydrolysates as a substrate for enzymatic hydrolyses is not recommended, due to low saccharification efficiency and low ethanol yields.
the dilute acid pretreated rye straw can be effectively converted into bioethanol using SHF and SHCF processes.
